instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Here We Go Again
cards.instruction: Use every new disagreement to prove the same relationship pattern is repeating, then raise the consequences.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A cancellation goes in the dinner chat before seven. Not at eleven, when I'm scraping it into the bin. We've covered this.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My battery died this time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then use the office phone. Please distinguish an obstacle from having no options. Tomorrow I serve at seven and clear at eight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll borrow a phone. Just leave my plate in the oven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. That is how last Tuesday's dinner stayed warm until bedtime. From tomorrow, put your own meal in the oven. Uncooked.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've cancelled Sunday after Mum made the bed again. When a shift changes, you tell the host first. Please ring her.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She'll think I don't want to visit. Could you soften it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's what I did last month. You disappeared and I explained. This time, start with 'I'm sorry' and give her another date.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't know my next free Sunday. Can you check with her later?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. Put a reminder in your phone for when the rota arrives. Please enter it now. I'm not booking your next visit or explaining why there isn't one.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Let Me Lean
cards.instruction: Get someone to carry part of the emotional burden without making you name how heavy it has become.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you cancel our anniversary table? The number's on the fridge. Please make the call for me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Of course. I'll tell them something's come up and ask to move it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cancel, not move. Don't leave them expecting another date. Give my name and tonight's time; they don't need the reason.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Would speakerphone help? You could tell me if I miss anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No speaker, please. If you need to ask me something, cover the mouthpiece. Stay beside me, though.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Open the hospital envelope, please. Tear the short edge so you don't catch the letter. Read the first line before I do.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Shall I read it aloud?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First read it to yourself. Then tell me whether I should sit down. Calmly, please; don't do that sharp breath people do.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sit beside me. We can read it one line at a time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. Keep your finger under the words, not over them. I'll follow. Slowly, please. I'm quite capable of reading; just keep your hand there.

cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Stay Until I’m Steady
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until you feel steady enough to face what comes next without them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay while I practise telling the children about tomorrow's operation. Sit where they will sit, please. This needs to be a proper rehearsal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Do you want me to ask whether you'll die?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not in that tone. Use their voices, please. I need to answer without snapping before I bring them in.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can do one question. My taxi's outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then ask that one again, quietly. Don't reach for your coat until I've finished the answer. Then I'll fetch the children.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you leave me in this new flat, count five breaths with me. Start again, please; I can't keep up with that count.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Five. Shall I shut the door?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not while I'm still looking at you. We should have done this facing the kitchen. Stand beside me; we'll repeat it correctly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll wait here while you put the kettle on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Stay until it boils, please. No, leave your cup in the box. I need to manage making just mine before you go.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Understand the Hurt
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge why their action hurt, not merely agree that it happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you apologise for missing my concert, tell me what you think you're apologising for. We need to get this right.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said I'd come, and work ran late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the sequence of events. Please try the part where I looked at your empty seat before every song. You'd heard me practise for months.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You wanted someone there who knew how hard you'd worked.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Keep that in the apology. Not 'sorry I was late'; you weren't there to hear what all that practice became.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I texted that I'd lost my job and you replied, 'What's for dinner?' Before you apologise, read those messages in order.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought something normal would help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's your intention. We're discussing what you asked of me. Please look at the question: who's apparently supposed to make dinner?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant we could go out. I'll book somewhere.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the booking for a moment. Can you say, 'It sounded as though I still expected you to cook'? We need that part before we choose a restaurant.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Tell Me I Did Enough
cards.instruction: Get someone to reassure you that your effort, choice, or survival was enough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only one of my paintings is ready for our exhibition. Before we hang anything, tell me whether I've contributed enough.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll spread mine out. Nobody will notice a gap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's display management, not an assessment of the work. Look at my painting, please. Does it belong here?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: In the middle. It's the first one I want people to see.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then introduce me as the other painter. No qualifications about how hard the year was, please. Just my name, beside yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I stayed at the lectern until the end of the speech. In your feedback, start with whether that was enough.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You left out a paragraph.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's a content note. Please keep it separate. I'm asking whether getting through it without walking away counts as a finished job.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It does. I'll help you practise the missing paragraph tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then please cross tomorrow's practice off. If it was a finished job, I need you to let me put the pages away.
